title: Goal Setting and Life Planning
summary: Setting SMART personal, academic and career goals, action plans and life plans, overcoming barriers, and the role of motivation, persistence and support networks.

notes.text: Grade 11 marks are often used for **provisional university admission**, so planning now is important. Goals give direction, motivation and a way to measure progress.

rows: by doing extra practice and attending Saturday classes

notes.title: An action plan
notes.problem: Goal: be accepted for a Diploma in IT at a university of technology for the year after matric.
steps: Research entry requirements (APS and minimum Mathematics mark) by March.
Improve Mathematics by 10% by June through weekly tutoring.
Apply for NSFAS and bursaries when applications open in Grade 12.
Gain experience: complete a free online coding course during the holidays.
notes.answer: Each step has a deadline, resources and a way to measure success.

rows: Bursaries, NSFAS, part-time work, free online resources
Career centres, LO teacher, open days, websites
Break goals into small steps, reward progress, find a mentor
Time management, ask for support, community resources
Learn from mistakes, adjust the plan, ask for help

notes.label: Resilience
notes.text: Successful people still face setbacks. **Resilience** (bouncing back), **persistence** and a strong **support network** of family, friends, mentors and teachers make the difference.

questions.prompt: What does the T in SMART stand for?
Grade 11 results are often used for provisional university admission.
Rewrite the goal 'I want to do better at school' as a SMART goal.
questions.memo:
✓ Specific subject/target (1)
✓ Measurable mark and method (1)
✓ Time-bound deadline (1)

questions.prompt: Name TWO barriers to achieving a career goal and suggest a strategy to overcome each.
What is the ability to bounce back after setbacks called?
What THREE elements should an action plan include?
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): specific steps; deadlines; resources needed; people who can help; ways to measure progress

questions.prompt: Why is a support network important when working towards long-term goals?
questions.memo:
✓ It provides encouragement and motivation (1)
✓ and practical help, advice and information when facing setbacks (1)

questions.prompt: A learner fails a test after studying hard. Describe TWO constructive responses.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): analyse mistakes; ask the teacher for help; adjust study methods; set a new goal; avoid giving up

options: an experienced person who guides and advises you
